A1.justification: Both PDFs describe PoseMaster's image-and-skeleton-conditioned 3D generation framework. Their complete main texts, equations, tables, figures and appendices are readable and support reliable comparison despite substantial revisions.

before.justification: v1 reports original geometric evaluations on Playbox and VRoid, generation timings, pose-representation and guidance ablations, and qualitative generation results.

after.justification: v2 reports original canonicalization and arbitrary-pose comparisons, skeleton-guidance experiments, generation timings, robustness tests and additional qualitative evaluations.

M1.justification: v1's fine-tuned Dora VAE and separately trained DiT are replaced by a pretrained Hunyuan3D 2.1 backbone with frozen VAE. Bone-endpoint tokens become densified coordinate-and-direction points, sampled to 256 points and encoded by two point-transformer blocks. Hand bones are incorporated. The documented four-condition guidance becomes skeleton-conditioned two-branch guidance. The data-construction procedure also adds automatically rigged static assets and view pairs.

E1.justification: Training expands from Playbox-derived AnimePose to diverse animated and static humanoids from ReadyPlayerMe, VRoid, Objaverse, Objaverse-XL and HumanRig. Evaluation adds real photographs from DeepFashion and deliberately mismatched skeleton proportions/topologies. The separately reported Playbox quantitative benchmark disappears. CharacterGen's test set and synthetic-image examples already existed in v1 and are expanded or revised, rather than entirely new coverage.

E2.justification: v2 adds Hunyuan3D 2.1 to the canonicalization comparison and introduces arbitrary-pose comparisons against Trellis, CraftsMan and Hunyuan3D, including Qwen-Image-to-3D cascades. v1's qualitative Mixamo comparison is removed. CharacterGen and StdGen remain canonicalization and timing comparators; SKDream is discussed but not experimentally evaluated.

E3.justification: CD, Fidelity Distance and F1 are replaced by normal-map MAE/SIM and Uni3D-I/ULIP-I. Appendix 9.1 selects the best normal-map score over 36 ground-truth azimuths. Canonicalization now specifies 50 VRoid images, replacing the earlier Playbox/VRoid benchmark specification. New arbitrary-pose protocols give baselines ground-truth or Qwen-edited target-pose images, while PoseMaster receives a source image and target skeleton. These settings preclude direct cross-version score comparisons.

E4.justification: The joint-versus-bone study becomes a sparse-joint-versus-dense-point study. v2 adds an image-only versus skeleton-guided comparison, mismatched-skeleton robustness cases, and ground-truth versus Qwen-edited baseline-input analysis. It removes v1's CFG-strategy ablation and 10–90-degree arm-angle demonstration. Thus both the questions investigated and their supporting evidence change substantially.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests. Both present point estimates and qualitative examples without statistical uncertainty estimates.

E6.justification: The canonicalization result rows are replaced under different metrics, and v2 adds quantitative arbitrary-pose, skeleton-guidance and Qwen-cascade results in Tables 2–4. Reported timings change from approximately 3/60/180 seconds to 23.48/32.98/61.54 seconds for PoseMaster/CharacterGen/StdGen, respectively (v1 Table 2; v2 Table 5). Numerous qualitative results also change. These are revised results under changed or newly specified conditions, not controlled cross-version performance gains or losses.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions of the pose condition and guided vector field change: endpoint-based encoding and four-condition guidance in v1 are replaced by coordinate/direction encoding and skeleton-conditioned guidance in v2 (v1 Equations 4 and 8; v2 Equations 3 and 4). The flow-matching objectives remain equivalent, and neither version introduces theorem or proof results.

C1.justification: The unified image-and-skeleton generation claim remains, but headline contributions shift substantially. v2 drops independent condition masking and implicit skeleton-to-skinning learning as central contributions, emphasizes a scalable mixed-asset data engine, extends superiority claims to arbitrary-pose comparisons, and foregrounds skeleton-aligned asset generation for animation without manual retargeting.

C2.justification: v2 emphasizes dense structural priors, depth ambiguity and skeleton–mesh alignment as explanations for control and animation applicability, replacing much of v1's learned-physical-prior and CFG-generalization discussion. Limitations change from absent hand guidance and restricted data/model scale to difficult hand, hair and skirt details and the single-stage 512-resolution output. Texture mismatch remains acknowledged, with external editing, refinement and texturing now discussed as mitigation.

D1.justification: v2 documents pretrained/frozen components, interpolation and sampling details, encoder dimensions, synchronized augmentations, a 3:2 dynamic/static data ratio, UniRig-based skeleton extraction, static-view rendering and single-H20 timing hardware. The stated learning rate changes from 1e-4 to 1e-5. Conversely, v1's explicit training GPU count, DiT layer/parameter counts, VAE latent length and several rendering/sampling settings are no longer supplied for the revised system.

R1.justification: The broad SDS/LRM and character-generation survey is replaced by sections on 2D pose stylization, 3D pose stylization and native 3D generation. Substantial new discussion covers video animation, Qwen-Image, SKDream, newer native generators and UniRig/Puppeteer. The work is additionally positioned as a controllable alternative to skeleton-prediction-based rigging.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, introduction, related work, method explanations and conclusion are extensively rewritten around pose stylization. Experimental sections are reorganized, animation receives a main-text Application section, and the appendix becomes separate Additional Details, Additional Experimental Results, and Limitation and Discussion sections.

P2.justification: v2 redraws the teaser and pipeline, adds data-engine, skeleton-densification and animation diagrams, restructures numerical tables, and redesigns qualitative comparisons with additional baseline and ground-truth columns. CFG, Mixamo and arm-angle panels disappear. The timing table moves to the appendix, while the existing 3D-printing diagram is retained and expanded with additional examples.

improvement.justification: v1's central arbitrary-pose capability relied mainly on visual examples and a Mixamo comparison with unmatched poses. v2 adds quantitative comparisons using both ground-truth and edited baseline inputs, explicit metric computation, real-photo evaluations and mismatched-skeleton tests. This substantially strengthens evidence for the paper's central purpose. Uncertainty reporting remains absent, and training/test separation is less explicit after VRoid enters training. These limitations temper the gains, and changed metrics and backbones prevent a controlled cross-version performance conclusion.
